name: independent-install-negatives
reviewer: Independent reviewer (Claude Opus 5 CLI documentation review seat)

steps.action: A missing key is refused before any container changes
steps.actual: Blanking AUTH_SECRET in .env made both docker compose config --quiet and docker compose up -d exit 1 with "required variable AUTH_SECRET is missing a value: AUTH_SECRET is required — generate one with `openssl rand -base64 32` and set it in .env". docker compose ps still showed app, worker, postgres and doc-engine up, so Compose refused the command without touching the running installation.

steps.action: Restoring the intended key returns the installation to readiness
steps.actual: Putting the generated AUTH_SECRET back made docker compose config --quiet exit 0 and /readyz answered 200 again.

steps.action: An occupied host port fails the start and names the port
steps.actual: Setting PORT=43333, a port an unrelated owned preview server was already listening on, made docker compose up -d exit 1 with "failed to bind host port 0.0.0.0:43333/tcp: address already in use". The unrelated listener was left alone. The failed recreate left the installation without its app and worker containers: docker compose ps then listed only doc-engine and postgres.

steps.action: Choosing an unused port again recovers the instance
steps.actual: Restoring PORT=43360 and running docker compose up -d --no-build --pull never brought app and worker back and /readyz answered 200.
